samples: This program reads a fixed file, data/sales.csv, and checks that every row has a region, a product and a numeric amount. If any row is bad, it stops with an error naming the line and the problem. Otherwise it adds up the amounts for each region, prints the regional totals from highest to lowest, and saves them in the same order to a two-column CSV report at data/report.csv. It only touches the data folder and the console, and the paths are hardcoded, so it suits a quick report on that one file but not a reusable tool. The product column is checked but never used in the totals.

This program reads `data/sales.csv`, checks that every row has a region, product and numeric amount, and adds up the amounts for each region. It prints the totals to the console, largest first, and saves them as a two-column CSV report at `data/report.csv`. It is all-or-nothing: a single bad row, an unreadable file or a failed write stops the run with an error (bad rows are reported with their line number), so no report is produced from partial data. File access is limited to the `data` folder, and the input path and output path are fixed rather than configurable.

This program reads a fixed sales file (`data/sales.csv`) and checks that every row has a region, product and numeric amount, stopping with the offending line number at the first bad row. It then adds up the amounts for each region, prints the regions to the console from highest total to lowest, and writes the same figures to a `data/report.csv` file. It is a simple, single-purpose tool with hard-coded file locations, and it is limited to the console and the `data` folder, so you would need to change it for other file names or for a report that skips bad rows instead of failing.

This program reads `data/sales.csv`, checks that every row has a region, a product and a numeric amount, and adds up the amounts for each region. It prints the regional totals from largest to smallest and saves them to `data/report.csv` with a header line. It stops at the first bad row, reporting the line number and the problem, or at any file or CSV read or write error, so it never produces a partial report, and it only touches the `data` folder and the console.

This program reads a fixed file, data/sales.csv, and checks that every row has a region, a product and a numeric amount. It stops with an error naming the line number as soon as any row is bad or the file can't be read or parsed. Otherwise it adds up the amounts for each region, prints the regions from highest to lowest total, and writes the same totals to data/report.csv, replacing any existing report. It touches only the data folder and the console, with no network access, but the input and output paths are hardcoded and the file must contain region, product and amount columns.
